conflict_synopsis.core_view: Hot US demand/labor plus a confirmed tightening bias leave December 2026 SOFR too low versus a shallow +34.75bp path.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Next US inflation/labor print or FOMC communication that forces more than one extra 2026 hike into SR1Z26.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: Fed tightening bias dropped and Dec-26 implied SOFR falls back toward unchanged 3.85 SOFR policy.

remit: underpriced hawkish policy, higher terminal rates, or higher-rate repricing
stance_summary: Inflation persistence and still-hot US demand/labor mean the Fed’s just-delivered hike is not the end of the tightening impulse. The live 1M SOFR path only prices about one extra hike by December 2026 and then a shallow peak near 4.72% with 2028 easing, which underprices the reaction function. Express that as paying December 2026 SOFR, not as a USD-spot default.

catalysts: Next US CPI/labor prints testing whether the August tightening-bias signal persists.
Subsequent FOMC communication versus a path that only prices SR1Z26 4.1975.
Energy-pass-through and shock-absorber headlines versus the Saudi workaround that cut the extreme oil tail.
Global confirmation: further BoJ/BoE hawkish residuals that keep term-rate pressure elevated.

The closing mechanism is additional 2026 hike pricing and a higher 2027 peak/delayed 2028 easing in the 1M SOFR strip. historical_reference.regime_differences: 2022 analogs started from much lower yield levels (2.13 then 3.85) in a first-ascent inflation shock with policy still far behind; today the funds target is already 3.75–4.00% and cash 2Y is 4.76, so remaining hike convexity is smaller. The 2023-02 analog included a US banking-stress unwind that is not in this packet; the current overlay is an energy shock plus BoJ/BoE hawkish confirmation. Packet SOFR method is delayed ICE 1M averages, not 2022 FOMC-probability screens. Do not pool those episodes as a mechanical +40–88bp 3m forecast.

context_build.known_vs_new_information: Known before the cutoff: August CPI kept Fed tightening bias intact (rollup 11 Sep); markets entered 16 Sep with >90% odds of a 25bp hike; the hike to 3.75–4.00% was then delivered. New after that known hike: BoJ to 1.25% on 17 Sep; BoE held 3.75% but with three votes for a hike; desk thesis 18 Sep that the energy shock is constraining the global easing impulse; energy-market shock absorbers weaken, even as a Saudi Oman ship-to-ship workaround reduced the extreme oil-supply tail. The 1M SOFR strip still only prices +34.75bp by Dec-26. Inference: the new information is global confirmation of tightening breadth, not the existence of the Fed hike.
context_build.market_assumption_disagreed_with: Disagreement: that the Sep-16 hike plus one more 2026 move and a sub-4.75% 2027 peak is enough given still-hot US labor/consumer/activity and a live energy-inflation tail. The hawk case is more 2026 hikes and a higher/later terminal, so Dec-26 implied SOFR and the 2027 peak are too low and the 2028 dip is premature.
context_build.market_implied_assumption: The 1M SOFR strip requires roughly one additional 25bp-scale move by December 2026 (Dec implied 4.1975 versus SOFR 3.85 and a 3.75–4.00% target range) and a cycle peak only 4.7225 in Dec-27, then slight easing toward 4.6025 by Aug-28. That is a shallow extra ~87bp over 15 months, then a modest 2028 downshift. Method caveat verified: these are 100 minus delayed ICE 1M SOFR prices, monthly-average SOFR, not meeting probabilities.
context_build.path_to_current_price: Verified policy path (delayed ICE 1M SOFR via eSignal, monthly-average SOFR, not FOMC target probabilities): SOFR 3.85 as_of 2026-09-17; SR1U26 Sep implied 3.75 (price 96.25, -10.0bp from overnight); SR1V26 Oct 3.91 (+6.0bp); SR1X26 Nov 4.045 (+19.5bp); SR1Z26 Dec 4.1975 (price 95.8025, +34.75bp); then a grind to SR1Z27 Dec-27 4.7225 (+87.25bp) before SR1U28 Aug-28 4.6025, which the packet labels terminal. Pre-decision, interest-rate futures priced greater-than-90% probability of the 25bp hike, so the Sep-16 move itself was largely known. After the decision, BoJ hiked 25bp to 1.25% (7–2) and the last24 desk (18 Sep) framed global tightening as broadening, while US 2Y stands at 4.76 and 10Y at 5.01 as_of 2026-09-18 (1y pctiles 99.8015873015873 and 99.60317460317461). Unknown: tick-level path of SR1Z26 on 16–18 Sep and whether delayed eSignal prints lag the live ICE/CME surface.

policy_path_check.rationale: Inspected US SOFR-linked, CA CORRA-linked, and AU AONIA/ASX cash-futures paths before sovereign 2Y/5Y or CA-US/AU-US RV. Selected US 1M SOFR because US demand/labor heat plus a just-confirmed tightening bias is the cleanest hawkish reaction-function gap: Dec-26 only +34.75bp. Rejected CA 1M-only +29bp as the headline underpricing because the 3M CORRA strip already prices ~136bp of hikes and CA labor 38 / core near 2% cap the near-term BoC case. Rejected paying AU cash futures as primary despite Inflation 82 because NSW stamp-duty receipts -24% y/y, transactions -18%, and Sydney/Melbourne values >7% from peak show the tightening channel already biting, and Dec AU futures liquidity is 2 contracts of volume. Did not substitute US 2Y 99.8th percentile for the SOFR path.

context_build.price_decomposition: Level versus change on the policy path, not the US 2Y percentile. Overnight benchmark SOFR 3.85. Near-dated Sep contract 3.75 is a month-end monthly-average residual around a mid-month hike, not a dovish signal. The marginal priced tightening is concentrated in Nov–Dec 2026 (+19.5bp then +34.75bp versus overnight). Belly/peak is Dec-27 4.7225. Packet terminal is the last listed contract Aug-28 4.6025, which is below the peak, i.e. a small easing tail. Sovereign 2Y 4.76 already sits near that 2027 peak, so cash 2Y is not a substitute for the underpriced 2026 1M strip. 2s10s is 25.0bp as_of 2026-09-18 (1y pctile 0.1984126984126984), a flat curve consistent with front-end tightness already in cash yields, not with a fully priced 2026 SOFR path.

trade.invalidation: Thesis is wrong if subsequent US inflation/labor data and FOMC communication drop the tightening bias, or if the 1M SOFR strip reprices SR1Z26 implied SOFR down toward unchanged policy at the 3.85 SOFR benchmark rather than higher. Delayed eSignal versus live ICE basis is a mark risk, not an invalidation of the macro claim.
trade.mispricing: SR1Z26 at 4.1975 versus SOFR 3.85 prices only about one additional 25bp-scale move by December after a hike that was already >90% priced. The hawkish residual — another 2026 hike and/or a higher 2027 peak — is not in the 2026 1M contract. US 2Y 4.76 is a different tenor and is already near the 2027 peak; it is not this mispricing.
principal_risks: The Sep-16 hike was >90% priced; remaining 2026 SOFR convexity may be only 10–20bp if the Fed hikes once more and stops.
Saudi workaround and any further oil-supply relief can fade the energy-inflation tail.
US 2Y already 4.76 / 99.8th 1y percentile: cash duration has already moved; a growth scare can rally the strip without invalidating long-run inflation (2023-02 analog).
Packet SOFR path is delayed eSignal ICE 1M, not CME/FOMC probabilities; AU OIS is stale; NZ rates unavailable; CFTC trader-class nets null; no executable broker prices.
CA 3M CORRA already prices a long hiking grind, so a US-versus-Canada rates RV is not this trade and can go the other way if BoC catches up.
trade.structure: Short/pay ICE 1-month SOFR future SR1Z26. Packet research/reference: implied_rate 4.1975, price 95.8025, source ESIGNAL_ICE_1M_SOFR_DELAYED. Not an executable broker ticket.
trade.thesis: Verified fact: Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75–4.00%; August CPI kept tightening bias intact; SOFR 3.85; SR1Z26 implies 4.1975 (+34.75bp); US gauges Inflation 72 / Labor 75 / Activity 69 / Consumer 74; BoJ hiked to 1.25%; BoE 6–3 with three hike votes. Inference: that configuration is not consistent with a 2026 path that only prices one extra hike and a 4.7225 peak. Paying Dec-26 SOFR owns the near-term hike underpricing that cash 2Y at 4.76 does not isolate. Unknown: next US CPI composition, unobserved SOFR meeting-implied probabilities, and whether delayed eSignal is off the live ICE mark.
